objective: Add the AI cover generation flow and its HTTP handler, with every AWS and storage call injected.
deliverable: Reviewable pull request with passing tests; no merge or deployment.
requirements: Create src/lib/ai-cover-service.ts exactly as specified in the acceptance test header, following the existing description pattern (generateDescription in src/lib/description-generation.ts and descriptionRequest in src/lib/description-http.ts): load any saved attempt first, never invoke the model twice for one attempt id, reserve before the paid call, and keep failed attempts consumed.

Reuse existing helpers, importing each with its explicit .ts extension so Node tests can load it: buildCoverRequest(title: unknown, style: unknown) and parseCoverResponse(body: unknown) from ./ai-cover.ts (shown); coverGenerationId(owner: unknown, item: unknown, style: unknown): string from ./ai-cover-budget.ts (64 lowercase hex, throws for invalid input); sameOrigin(request: Request): boolean and boundedJson(request: Request): Promise<unknown> (throws for a non-JSON content type, over 20000 bytes or invalid JSON) from ./description-http.ts. The last two modules are not shown and must not be changed. Use node:crypto for SHA-256.

Every AWS, DynamoDB and Supabase call is supplied by the injected backend; this module must not import AWS SDKs, Supabase or React, and must not read files, the network or process.env directly (the handler receives env as a parameter).
Error replies use fixed messages only; never include exception or provider text in a response.
src/lib/ai-cover.ts is provided for reference and must not be changed; the existing ai-cover and ai-cover-budget acceptance tests must keep passing.
Keep the change small: one module and one focused test file; a repair should change only what its findings require.
acceptance_tests_note: Factory-owned tests run unchanged in the sandbox after the repository checks, together with the existing ai-cover acceptance tests; the builder cannot edit them and must make them pass.
source_manifest_note: Computed by the coding assistant from a separate read-only clone with both the Factory reader and the owner's standalone script (113 files, 708558 bytes); the Factory fetch verifies it independently before use.
